title: Contrast-enhanced liver ultrasound
what: This is a liver ultrasound where a special contrast made of tiny gas bubbles is given into a vein. It lets the doctor see how blood fills spots in the liver.
why: To find out what a spot in the liver is, after it was seen on a regular ultrasound, CT, or MRI, and for follow-up after liver treatment.
duration: usually 20 to 40 minutes including preparation; the report is usually ready the same day
tell_doctor: Allergies, especially any past reactions to contrast
Heart and lung conditions, especially if they recently got worse
If you are pregnant or breastfeeding

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually 4 to 6 hours without food. Still water is fine. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

prepare.title: Kidneys
prepare.text: This contrast does not harm the kidneys, so kidney tests are usually not needed. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: After the scan, you are usually asked to stay at the clinic for about 30 minutes.

bring: Past liver ultrasound, CT, and MRI results
steps: The nurse puts a thin tube, a cannula, into a vein in your arm
You lie on your back, and gel is put on your belly
The doctor first looks at the liver with regular ultrasound
A small amount of contrast is given through the cannula
The doctor watches the spot for a few minutes. Sometimes you are asked to hold your breath
The cannula is taken out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick when the cannula goes in
You usually do not feel the contrast. Sometimes there is mild warmth or a strange taste
Rarely, a mild headache or nausea. Tell the doctor
after: You usually stay under watch for about 30 minutes
Then you can eat and go back to your day
The report is usually ready the same day
Your doctor will talk about the next plan
red_flags: A rash, itching, or swelling of the face or lips: tell the doctor right away
Trouble breathing, chest pain, or severe weakness: call emergency services if you are already home

faq.q: Is this contrast the same as for CT?
faq.a: No. It has no iodine. It leaves the body through the lungs when you breathe and does not strain the kidneys.

faq.q: Can you be allergic to this contrast?
faq.a: Rarely. That is why you are watched at the clinic for a short time after the scan.

reminders.text: Contrast liver ultrasound tomorrow. Do not eat for 4 to 6 hours before. Still water is fine. Bring your past scans.
